title: Optional usage
concept: Optional explicitly expresses ‘there may be no value’ instead of null.

steps.title: Optional.of() - Create a box
steps.explanation:
**What happens in memory:**
Create a **hard wrapper** called `Optional` on the heap and safely place the string "hello" inside the box.

**Warning:** `of()` never allows `null`.
If you enter null, an NPE will occur before the box is even created.

steps.title: Optional.empty() - empty box
steps.explanation:
Creates an 'empty box' object with no content.
Instead of using a `null` variable, this is a way to clearly say "I have a box, but no content."
Returning `Optional` lets you know right away, “Oh, maybe it’s not there.”

steps.title: Optional.ofNullable() - flexible box
steps.explanation:
If the value is present, it is placed in a box (`of`). If it is `null`, an empty box is created (`empty`).
In reality, this is the most commonly used creation method.

steps.title: get() - force eject (dangerous!!)
steps.explanation:
I open the box blindly.
I'm glad I have the value now, but if I call `get()` when it's empty, it throws a **`NoSuchElementException`** exception.

**Warning:** `get()` is a last resort.
Avoid using it as much as possible.
steps.keyInsight: Recommended to use orElse() instead of get()

steps.title: isPresent() - Check
steps.explanation:
It asks "Does the box have a value?" (`isPresent`).
Since `opt2` is empty, it returns `false`, and the `if` block is not executed.

javaMemoryState.note: opt2 is empty so returns false, block is not executed

steps.title: orElse() - Provides safe default values
steps.explanation:
**Most recommended method:** “Open the box.
If there is a value, use that. **If it is empty, use 'default' instead.**"
You can get the value neatly and safely in one line.

javaMemoryState.note: opt3 is empty so "default" is returned

steps.title: ifPresent() - functional style
steps.explanation:
“If there is a value, execute this function (lambda).
“Not if you don’t have it.”
It's an elegant way to do things inside the box without pulling out the values.
steps.keyInsight: ifPresent() = Executes only when there is a value

javaMemoryState.note: opt1 has a value so the lambda is executed

quiz.question: Where should I not use Optional?
quiz.explanation:
Optional is designed only for method returns.
If you use it as a field, it will waste a lot of memory and cause serialization problems.

misconceptions.correct:
no.
The Optional variable itself may be null (worst case scenario).
misconceptions.why: To use Optional, you should never use `Optional<String> opt = null;` and always initialize it with `Optional.empty()`.

misconceptions.wrong: The isPresent() + get() pattern is standard.
misconceptions.correct: Using methods such as `orElse()` or `ifPresent()` is an ‘optional’ usage.
misconceptions.why:
`if (opt.isPresent()) { ... get() }` is no different from `if (x != null)`, which makes the code verbose.
The true value of Optional lies in its functional style.

keyTakeaway: Optional for return type, orElse() when taken out!
